summary: I walked the spec steps 1–15 of String.prototype.replace against the diff, along with the helpers StringIndexOf and GetSubstitution. Every step is implemented in order with `?` on the fallible operations: RequireObjectCoercible, GetMethod on @@replace with Call, ToString(this) before ToString(searchValue), IsCallable before the conditional ToString(replaceValue), and the functional-replace Call with (searchString, position, string). The non-functional path calls GetSubstitution with empty captures and no namedCaptures. In that case the spec leaves `$n` and `$<` as literal text, and the implementation does the same. `$$`, `` $` ``, `$&` and `$'` match the spec's substring rules, including the min(tailPos, stringLength) clamp. StringIndexOf's empty-search and out-of-range cases match the spec, and the slices are bounds-safe. The gate shows no regressions. The remaining failures are the honest not-implemented error for RegExp.prototype.hasIndices. Nothing is special-cased. The only thing I would flag, and it is not one of the questions, is that GetSubstitution and StringIndexOf are written as file-local helpers. The ticket permits this, but GetSubstitution is also needed by replaceAll and RegExp @@replace, so it may belong in ops.
